subject: health
title: Heart, Lungs and Bones
about: The heartbeat he can feel, the heart in the chest beating faster when he runs, lungs filling with air and why he breathes hard after a race, blood carrying food and air, the skeleton, skull and ribs, calcium from milk, muscles moving the body and growing stronger with use, endurance, and rest after hard play. NC 1.NPA.2.1 (activities good for the body) and PE.1.HF.3.1 and PE.1.HF.3.2 (fitness parts and the benefits of activity) with 1.NPA.1.2 (why we eat certain foods); builds on Move Your Body.
tip: Have him feel his heartbeat sitting still, then do 20 jumping jacks and feel it again.

cards.q: Put your hand on your chest. What is the thump, thump you feel?
cards.note: Your heart beats all day and all night, even while you sleep.

cards.q: Where in your body is your heart?
cards.note: It sits in the middle of your chest, a little to the left, and is about the size of your fist.

cards.q: You run fast across the yard. What does your heart do?
cards.note: A faster heartbeat sends more blood to your busy muscles.

cards.q: What carries food and air to every part of your body?
cards.note: The heart pumps blood through tiny tubes called blood vessels.
Lungs pull air in and push it out, many times every minute.

cards.q: Take a big breath in. What fills up with air?
cards.note: Lungs stretch like two balloons when you breathe in.

cards.q: How many lungs do you have?
cards.note: One on the left and one on the right, inside your chest.

cards.q: Which parts of your body let air in?
cards.note: Air goes in your nose or mouth, down a tube called the windpipe, and into your lungs.

cards.q: After a race you breathe hard and fast. Why?
cards.note: Working muscles need extra air, so your lungs work harder too.

cards.q: What holds your body up and gives it its shape?
cards.note: Without bones you would be floppy like a jellyfish.

cards.q: All the bones in your body together are called your...?
cards.note: A grown-up has 206 bones. Kids have even more, and some join together as you grow.

cards.q: Which bone is a hard helmet for your brain?
cards.note: The skull keeps your brain safe. A bike helmet protects the skull.

cards.q: Which bones make a cage around your heart and lungs?
cards.note: Feel the ribs on the sides of your chest. You have twelve pairs.

cards.q: What in milk, cheese and yogurt helps bones grow strong?
cards.note: Bones keep growing until you are grown. Calcium helps make them hard and strong.
Muscles pull on bones to bend your arm, kick a ball or smile.
Climbing, carrying and pushing make muscles grow. Use them and they get stronger.

cards.q: You can run and play a long time without getting tired. Your heart and lungs have what?
cards.note: Endurance means keeping going. Running, biking and swimming build it.

cards.q: After hard play, what does your body need?
cards.note: Rest and sleep are when muscles and bones do their growing.
